text:
jordan: heads-up — saw a big tail-latency spike on /generate around 10:07 UTC, HPA shot to 30 replicas but most pods stayed Pending. App latency hit ~3.5s for ~15m.

nina: looking — pods Pending with "0/20 nodes available" and node affinity mismatch. Also seeing CA scale-up blocked logs.

jordan: pod describe excerpt:
```
Tolerations: node.kubernetes.io/gpu:NoSchedule
Node-Selectors: accelerator: nvidia
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/20 nodes available: 20 node(s) didn't match pod affinity/selector.
```

cory: CA says: \"scale-up suppressed: pool-gpu max nodes reached\" — pool-gpu max=10 current=10 according to autoscaler.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scale-up blocked: reached max nodes for nodepool pool-gpu (10).

jordan: odd — we hadn't been at capacity earlier. VPA recently applied and bumped container requests (recommendation applied last hour), that may have changed the external-metrics math used by the HPA.

nina: confirming — external-metrics adapter is publishing qps_per_pod = request_rate / target_cpu_estimate (was supposed to be request_rate / replicas). VPA changing requests makes the denominator wobble.

cory: TL;DR: HPA reacts to an unstable external metric, scales replicas up, but pods require GPU node affinity so CA would add nodes, except pool max blocks it. Result: Pending pods + latency.

jordan: immediate mitigations?

sre-oncall: i'll patch deployment to add toleration+nodeSelector for existing burst pool and manually increase pool-gpu max to 25 while we triage.

sre-oncall: patch applied, scaling pool max->25 now, creating 3 nodes in gpu-burst.

jordan: pods are starting to schedule. seeing warmup logs: 
```
2026-03-18T10:12:11Z pod/my-model-xyz Scheduling -> Running
2026-03-18T10:12:15Z container started, gpu visible: 0/1
```

nina: latency returning to baseline :thumbsup: — good call on manual bump. Longer term we should avoid tying HPA to a metric that VPA changes indirectly.

cory: agreed. Proposed follow-ups:
- fix external-metrics adapter to compute qps_per_pod = sum(request_rate) / max(1, replicas) with a 2m smoothing window
- add HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to 90s and a fallback metric (CPU% or request-rate-percentile)
- change VPA mode to \"auto\" with conservative updatePolicy (or set recommender only during off-peak)
- create a separate burst nodepool with taint gpu-burst:NoSchedule and autoscaler permission to scale beyond baseline for spikes
- add CA scale-up dry-run alert when pool max would block scale-ups

jordan: i'll open infra issue INV-428 with those action items and assign owners.

sre-oncall: will also add a short runbook step: when pods Pending + node-affinity -> check pool max and CA logs, and if necessary bump pool or create burst nodes.

nina: small config PR suggestion: change external-metrics adapter config snippet:
```
metric:
  name: qps_per_pod
  query: "sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m])) / max(1, sum(kube_deployment_status_replicas{deployment=~\"my-model.*\"}))"
  smoothing: 2m
```

cory: and maybe add pod anti-affinity to spread replicas across nodes so a single node warmup doesn't throttle all requests.

jordan: thanks everyone — pods stable, latency back under SLO. I'll link INV-428 here once it's created.

sre-oncall: nice work. marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
